core.title: Keep flow variables out of the FlowRouterRunner
core.given: A source module in the stack's user/system flows tree (profile: user/system flows tree) that defines a FlowRouterRunner (not the production FlowRunner module)
core.when: the module is created or changed
core.then: Keep flow variables inside FlowRunner execution: the FlowRouterRunner must not reference, mutate, store (artifact_urn -> artifact_data), or route on flow variables.
prefer: The FlowRouterRunner reads only the initial action/inputs/state before execution and a completed UserSystemFlowResult at a declared route boundary.
Leave flow variables to the FlowRunner, which passes it between product capabilities; product capabilities read and return artifact objects.
avoid: Flow-variable references or mutations of a flow-variable mapping in a FlowRouterRunner module.
Storing artifact_urn -> artifact_data runtime values in the flow router.
Routing on mid-train flow-variable state; letting flow variables select user/system flow variants.
unless: The production FlowRunner module legitimately constructs and carries flow variables; it is not scanned for flow-variable bleed.
core.why: Flow variables is the artifact data plane carried by the FlowRunner between product capabilities inside a selected user/system flow; the flow_variables_boundary keeps it inside that execution, so the flow router never routes on mid-train flow-variable state nor lets flow variables select user/system flow variants, routing only on initial inputs and declared-boundary UserSystemFlowResults.
evidence: The stack's flow-variable-boundary check reports no flow-variable reference, flow-variable-mapping mutation, or artifact_urn literal in any FlowRouterRunner-defining module in the user/system flows tree.

The same check reports no product capability entry module (located via the profile's product capability directory and capability-module pattern) importing flow router code — the companion split convention's obligation, enforced by the same realization check.

A reviewer confirms the FlowRouterRunner's routing inputs are only the initial action/inputs/state and declared-boundary UserSystemFlowResults, and that flow variables does not select user/system flow variants.
verification: Scan each FlowRouterRunner-defining module in the user/system flows tree and flag a flow-variable reference, a flow-variable-mapping mutation, or an artifact_urn literal.

Scan each product capability entry module (located via the profile's product capability directory and capability-module pattern) and flag an import of flow router code; that is the companion split convention's obligation, and one realization check may enforce it alongside this one — this core's then covers only the FlowRouterRunner flow-variable boundary.
Comment text is masked before matching; a string artifact_urn literal is still detected.
The production FlowRunner module is excluded from the flow-variable-bleed scan; only FlowRouterRunner-defining modules are scanned for flow-variable bleed.
Which modules are scanned and how flow-variable touches are recognized is the per-stack realization's (detector's) concern.
Severity 4, disposition strict: a newly introduced flow-variable touch (or, under the companion convention, a product capability importing flow router) is not suppressible and fails CI.

values: source module in the user/system flows tree
routing decision depends on mid-train flow-variable state

fires: A FlowRouterRunner module in the user/system flows tree references flow variables or assigns into a flow-variable mapping.
A FlowRouterRunner caches artifact_urn -> artifact_data values or contains an artifact_urn string literal.
A FlowRouterRunner chooses the next route from mid-train flow-variable state.
Flow-variable contents are used to select a user/system flow variant.
doesNotFire: The production FlowRunner module constructs flow variables and passes it between product capabilities.
A FlowRouterRunner reads the initial action/inputs/state before execution.
A FlowRouterRunner reads a completed UserSystemFlowResult at a declared route boundary.
A comment inside a FlowRouterRunner module mentions flow variables (comments are masked).

A product capability entry module (located via the profile's product capability directory and capability-module pattern) changes its imports (governed by the companion convention that product capabilities must not import flow router code).

neutralityNotes: FlowRunner, FlowRouterRunner, flow variables, artifact_urn/artifact_data, UserSystemFlowResult and product capability are the agnostic ATDD core-runtime spec's own vocabulary (the rule is the realization of the core 'flow variables boundary' obligation), so they are kept in the core. The Bun stack, the TypeScript/JavaScript languages (tooling.languages), the src/user-system-flows/** user/system flows tree (proposed roles.runtime_components#user_system_flows_location), and the src/<capability>/capability.ts capability-module location (layout.capability_dir plus proposed layout.locations#capability_module) all come from the profile; the `flowVariables[...] = ...` token form is generalized to 'flow-variable-mapping mutation' (the concrete form stays in bun.json as the reference example), and only the detector family/check-file ids and the companion split-convention rule id remain in bunOnly. The capability-must-not-import-flow-router half is the companion split convention's obligation; the core keeps it only as a generic, profile-parameterized note in evidence/verification so no extra obligation is added.
